rows: The sherriff's office relayed a report of nickel-size hail near Enloe.
Several trees and large limbs were blown down across the county.

Widespread wind damage was reported with numerous trees and power poles blown down. Some large trees were uprooted. A downburst likely caused the damage, which had a track of about two miles long by a mile and a half wide. Several roofs were ripped off businesses and residences, …
Large limbs were broken and fences were damaged.
The roof of a building on the west side of the square in Cooper collapsed. The incoming water broke the windows and doors, scattering debris onto Dallas Avenue.
Quarter to golfball sized hail fell in Klondike, which is approximately 4 miles southwest of Cooper.
Large trees were knocked down at the intersection of 4th Street and Terrell Ave. Power lines were also knocked down in the city of Cooper.
Quarter size hail was reported north of Klondike.

A sheriff's deputy estimated 60 MPH winds in Cooper.
Law enforcement reported tree damage in Cooper.
The Delta County Emergency Manager reported golf ball sized hail in the city of Cooper.
A trained spotter recorded a wind gust to the south of Cooper on Highway 24. Several trees were damaged in the vicinity.
Emergency management reported quarter sized hail in the city of Cooper, TX.
Emergency management reported half dollar sized hail in the city of Enloe, TX.
A social media report indicated ping pong ball sized hail in the city of Klondike, TX.

The same supercell that produced the earlier Cooper tornado moved northeast about 4 miles and spawned a second very brief tornado near Enloe, in northern Delta County. The tornado touched down in an open field just southeast of Enloe, destroying a couple of small outbuildings and…
The metal covering over a house roof was partially peeled off.
A home sustained damage on FM 64 southeast of Pecan Gap. The roof was damaged and water entered the home.
A large tree snapped and fell on the end of a manufactured home, damaging the roof of the home.

Strong thunderstorms damaged a property on Delta County Road 1120 peeling shingles off the roof, damaging outdoor furniture, peeling siding off an older home, and breaking wood paneling along a barn/garage.
A trained spotter reported trees down along Highway 19 near the South Sulphur River.
A social media picture indicated trees down near the intersection of FM 1531 and Highway 24, just south of Klondike, TX.

Spotter reported quarter-sized hail in northern Delta County along FM 128.
Spotter report of 2 inch hail in northern Delta County, along FM 128. This hail was wind-driven by 80 mph winds causing notable damage.
Photo received from the public of hail slightly larger than quarters just outside of Cooper.
